Open a Zarr store

Source: R/api.R
zaro.Rd

Connects to a Zarr store at the given path or URI. Dispatches to the appropriate backend based on the URI scheme:

  • Local paths: base R (no arrow or GDAL needed)

  • s3://, gs://: listed and read through Arrow when arrow is installed, else through GDAL's /vsis3/ or /vsigs/ (gdalraster). When access is known (anonymous, or S3 keys in the environment) chunks are fetched as HTTPS through the curl pool instead, see zaro_fetch()

  • http://, https://: curl (no GDAL); chunk reads are batched through one connection pool, see zaro_fetch(). An HTTP store can't be listed, so it needs consolidated metadata (or array names, see zaro_dataset())

  • /vsi...: any GDAL virtual file system path, through gdalraster (e.g. /vsicurl/https://... to keep GDAL's HTTP handling)

  • reference+json://: Kerchunk JSON reference store

  • reference+parquet://: Kerchunk Parquet reference store

  • virtualizarr://: VirtualiZarr Parquet manifest store

  • byterefs:// (or the older mdimrefs://): a byterefs SQLite byte-reference table (https://github.com/byterefs/spec), byterefs/0.1 or the legacy mdim-refs/0.2. Source paths are remapped for the store's meta.default_target; pass target = "public" for another target, or target = "" for the verbatim sources

  • flatrefs://: a byterefs flat refs store, the Parquet export (a directory, local or remote, with arrays.json and one refs_<array>.parquet per array, as raad.virtualize publishes). Chunk references are read by row group, only those whose dim statistics can hold the selection, so a table of tens of millions of rows is never read whole. target as for byterefs://

Usage

zaro(source, verbose = zaro_verbose(), ..., validate = FALSE)

Arguments

source

character. Path, URI, or reference store locator.

verbose

logical. Emit progress and diagnostic messages. Default getOption("zaro.verbose", TRUE); set options(zaro.verbose = FALSE) to silence zaro everywhere.

...

store options: for s3:// and gs://, arguments for the Arrow filesystem constructors (e.g. anonymous = TRUE, region, endpoint_override), also used for curl-pool access; for byterefs:// and flatrefs://, target (the path remap to apply).

validate

logical. Read the root metadata at open, warning if that fails. Default FALSE.

Value

A store object (internal class) for use with other zaro functions.

Details

For S3 stores, if Arrow returns a 301 redirect (wrong region), zaro will fall through to gdalraster's /vsis3/ which handles region detection automatically.

Known public buckets (e.g. cmip6, aodn-cloud-optimised) are accessed anonymously by default. For other public stores, pass anonymous = TRUE.

Opening reads nothing from the store by default (source is only checked to be a non-empty character string); set validate = TRUE to read the root metadata at open.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# local store
store <- zaro("/data/my_dataset.zarr")

# S3 store (anonymous)
store <- zaro("s3://mur-sst/zarr-v1", anonymous = TRUE)

# GCS - known public bucket, anonymous auto-detected
store <- zaro(paste0("gs://cmip6/CMIP6/ScenarioMIP/NOAA-GFDL/GFDL-ESM4/",
                     "ssp585/r1i1p1f1/Omon/zos/gn/v20180701"))

# VirtualiZarr Parquet reference
store <- zaro("virtualizarr://https://example.com/dataset.parq")

# byterefs: a SQLite table, or the flat Parquet export
store <- zaro("byterefs:///path/to/store.sqlite")
store <- zaro("flatrefs://https://example.com/store", target = "public")

# then explore
zaro_list(store)
zaro_meta(store, "analysed_sst")
data <- zaro_read(store, "analysed_sst",
                  start = c(0, 0, 0), count = c(1, 100, 100))
} # }
